newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Steel automotive steel share up 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: BHP Steel automotive steel share up 40 pct.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday its share of Australia's automotive steel market had increased nearly 40 percent since 1995.

"We've had some increase in market share in the automotive applications right across Australia since 1995, just under 40 increase in market share," Ron McNeily, executive general manager and chief executive officer of BHP's steel division told a briefing seminar.
McNeilly said BHP had recently won a deal to supply the Australian unit of Ford Motor Co with steel for its new model 1998 Ford Falcon.
"We will be supplying a major percentage of the steel to be used in the new Ford Falcon," McNeilly said.
BHP still had a long way to go to supply steel to the other major Australian car manufacturers, Toyota, Mitsubishi and General Motors Holden, but was making significant headway, he said.
"We believe their (Ford Australia's) plans for (export) growth in the Pacific Rim would factor in BHP as a potential steel supplier," he said.
"This means for the first time, we can be regarded as an international supplier of steel to the automotive market."
